questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Though an exchange is a lot of planning, I wouldn't ever be without it

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
One thing that you need to know about Sorbonne is that the institution does not communicate very well. Generally, we would get e-mails with direction on what to do and when. Ex when the information meetings would find place. But these e-mails came a few days before the meeting. So we spend a long time in the unknown, waiting for information about everything. 
To find information about classes and the likes is so difficult. They have several platforms for information (their webpage/ ENT / Moodle) and most of the information is inaccessible if you don't have a profile. Moodle is the most important one as it is here you find the pdf's with all the courses - which you need for the OLA

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
We had two meetings at Sorbonne 4. The first one introduced us to all the clubs and activities that are available. The second introduced us to everything surrounding the exchange(how/when to apply for classes, the different campuses, the different UFR's and so on).
It was possible to write e-mails to a coordinator but she was very french so make sure that you are polite and express yourself well if you communicate in e-mail with people.
They also wrote e-mails up until the exchange. You almost had to make a little treasure hunt to find the information that you needed - to be sure that you got everything. A lot of things are said implicit and the coordinator was very clear that it was an annoyance that people asked questions where the answer was available some place other than her. (I don't think everyone will have the same experience. She seemed very though)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found housing in the Cité Universitaire. As I got in, it was easy for me to get housing. I send it an application. I think that it was a motivated letter and a budget. 
When i talked to the directrice in the Danish house, she told me that around half of the applicants in the fall gets in so I don't know if I got lucky. It seems easier to get in in the spring

If you take classes on other campuses than Sorbonne 4/mère/the old one by the Luxembourg Garden, the transport time can be up to 50 min each way. I had classes at Malesherbes everyday and had between 30 and 45 min each way. I did not find this to be a problem at all as i don't mind the public transport system in Paris. Some might find it a bit much, but don't let it stop you from applying to the Cité

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be really hard to find your people when you are living on your own. I had friends who spend the first months being quite lonely but they found their friends in the end. its just more work that living with other people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I was swapped in the brassage program. between 30% and 50% of the students of each house are swapped into other houses. I think that the Danish house collaborates with around 10 houses that you can end up living in. I was swapped into the Swiss house and I really loved it. It is a great way of getting to know people from other countries and I learned so much about both Switzerland but also other countries. 
I indicated in my application that I would like to be swapped, so I'm sure that if I'd written that I'd had like to stay in the Danish house, that would have been possible.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
All courses were open to us so it is very hard to make a choice when you have hundreds of possibilities. 
You find the classes in pdf's on a different moodle that you use for classes during the year. 
you have full control over your classes so you can plan them when you want which is very nice.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
at my UFR we had to go to a room the friday before start of classes and write our wishes of classes on a piece of paper and hand it in to our erasmuscoordinator. 
then we had the first two weeks to try out classes before finalizing our choices. if we had changed anything we had to go to the office to change our paper

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: they had a presentation where they described the process otherwise we had to do everything by ourselves

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
it takes A LOT of time. 
you wont find all the information at the same place so you need to go hunting to make sure you get everything right

questions.answer: BA

questions.answer: i found the classes had a good level for me. you very much need good french comprehension skills, otherwise itll be difficult for you.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
it was very different. You are not expected to prepare for every class and you will have teachers who will start talking without telling you what is taught that day so you have no possibility of preparing. 

they teach for memory and not for using the information. so you are tested on what the teacher says and not ie your reading of an article because you will not be given the article - the teacher will describe it to you and you have to remember what they say.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
find other exchange students 
ask questions - to everyone who might help you 
record the classes/ask others for their notes
diversify your classes - not to many that are the same level/have too many books
there is a big jump between L2 and L3
many exams during the year - not preparation, they are by hand and no notes allowed

questions.answer: 7 exams in 7 days..... (17 exams during the semester)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
apply for grants 
the application work comes in waves - keep on top of e-mails 

it can be really difficult to find accomodation on the parisian market - look in danish groups. you cant completely trust everyone on the internet.
